concept.name: Dual-Tier Radix Prefix & HNSW Semantic Prompt Caching
concept.tagline: Cut LLM inference costs by 25–40% at <15 ms p99 without serving stale or cross-tenant hallucinations.
concept.purpose: Understand why naive string-hash LLM caches miss paraphrased queries, how L1 Radix prefix tries pair with L2 SQ8 HNSW cosine thresholding, and how entity guards prevent semantic drift.

prerequisites.title: Transformer KV-Cache & Prefill Physics
prerequisites.summary: Prefill attention scales quadratically with prompt length; reusing shared system-prompt KV blocks avoids redundant GPU FLOPs.

prerequisites.title: Cosine Similarity & HNSW Graphs
prerequisites.summary: Normalized dense embeddings measure semantic proximity via d(u, v) = 1 - (u · v), searchable in O(log N) via HNSW.

spark.summary: Exact string caching misses 85%+ of paraphrased LLM queries, while unguarded semantic vector caching risks serving inverted or cross-tenant answers.
spark.keyTakeaway: When serving foundation models with repetitive system prompts and paraphrased user queries, pair an L1 Radix-prefix hash tier (<1 ms) with a tenant-isolated L2 HNSW semantic tier gated by a calibrated cosine threshold (tau = 0.08) and lexical entity/negation guards so hit rates exceed 25% without hallucination drift.
spark.byteSummary:
Foundation model gateways waste massive GPU prefill and decode capacity re-computing identical system prompts and semantically equivalent user questions. Exact-key Redis caches capture verbatim repeats (~10–12% hit rate) but miss paraphrases like 'How do I reset MFA?' vs. 'Steps to reset multi-factor auth'.

A Dual-Tier Semantic & Prompt Cache resolves this in two stages. L1 hashes canonicalized 256-token prompt blocks with XXH3-64 inside an in-memory Radix Trie, returning exact hits in under 1 ms and emitting GPU KV-cache affinity hints on partial system-prompt matches. L1 misses flow into an ONNX INT8 embedding worker (<=4 ms) and a tenant-filtered SQ8 HNSW vector index (<=6 ms) gated by cosine distance tau = 0.08.

Because small lexical changes—such as 'enable' vs. 'disable' or 'Q3 2025' vs. 'Q3 2026'—still score close in embedding space, an Entity/Negation Slot Guard verifies exact numeric, date, and negation parity before returning a cached completion. Every entry carries a salted HMAC tenant namespace and a model_epoch tag for O(1) lazy invalidation.

learningJourney.title: P · Problem & Why Exact String Caching Breaks on Natural Language
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Quantifies the hit-rate ceiling of naive SHA-256 string caches and the semantic drift risk of uncalibrated vector caches.

explanation.foundation: In traditional web APIs, URLs are canonical keys. In LLM applications, two users asking 'Summarize Q3 churn drivers' and 'Give me the main reasons customers churned in Q3' have completely different SHA-256 hashes, resulting in a 0% exact-cache hit rate.
explanation.core: Conversely, dropping prompts blindly into a vector database with a loose threshold (tau = 0.20) causes catastrophic false positives: 'How do I delete my prod cluster?' can match 'How do I back up my prod cluster?'.
explanation.deepDive: At 5,000 sustained RPS (15,000 peak), even a 25% cache hit rate eliminates 1,250–3,750 GPU inference calls/sec—saving over 1M tokens/sec of HBM bandwidth—provided cache evaluation finishes within <15 ms p99.

learningJourney.title: R · Representation: Radix Prefix Trees & Normalized Vector Geometry
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Shows how L1 and L2 partition the prompt structure into deterministic prefix blocks and semantic user turns.

explanation.foundation: Every LLM prompt has two parts: a rigid prefix (system instructions, tool schemas, few-shot examples) and a fluid suffix (the user's natural-language question).
explanation.core: L1 stores 256-token prefix hashes in an in-memory Radix Trie keyed by HMAC(tenant_id, model_epoch). L2 embeds only the normalized user turn into a unit-normalized 384-d INT8 vector.
explanation.deepDive: Using 8-bit Scalar Quantization (SQ8) shrinks 100M 384-d vectors from 153.6 GB (FP32) to 38.4 GB in DRAM—fitting comfortably across 8 sharded HNSW nodes (RF=2 = 110.7 GB total DRAM including graph edges).

learningJourney.title: I · Invariant: Cosine Calibration Curve & Entity/Negation Slot Guard
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Prevents high-similarity lexical inversions from poisoning cached responses.

explanation.foundation: Embedding models capture broad topic similarity, not logical polarity. 'Enable audit logging' and 'Disable audit logging' often have cosine distance d = 0.06.
explanation.core: We enforce two invariants before serving an L2 hit: (1) d(u, v) < tau = 0.08, and (2) exact set equality on extracted numbers, dates, currency amounts, and negation tokens.
explanation.deepDive: If an incoming prompt contains '2026' or 'not' and the candidate cached prompt does not, the Slot Guard forces an immediate miss to the Foundation Model Origin.

learningJourney.title: M · Mechanics at Scale: Tenant Isolation & Lazy Epoch Invalidation
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Eliminates cross-tenant data leaks and thundering-herd flushes during model upgrades.

explanation.foundation: Every cache entry is prefixed with HMAC-SHA256(master_key, tenant_id) and indexed in HNSW with a Roaring Bitmap tenant filter so Tenant A can never retrieve Tenant B's vectors.
explanation.core: When model weights or system prompts change, bumping model_epoch in etcd/Redis invalidates stale entries in O(1) time on read without flushing 100M keys.
explanation.deepDive: Background RocksDB compaction filters automatically reclaim expired TTL and old-epoch records without blocking foreground reads.

learningJourney.title: E · Edge Cases, Assumptions & Glossary
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Defines operational boundaries, when NOT to use semantic caching, and core terminology.

explanation.foundation: Assumptions & Limitations: Semantic caching assumes deterministic or low-temperature (T <= 0.3) queries where approximate equivalence is acceptable. Never enable L2 semantic caching for creative writing, high-temperature brainstorming, or real-time volatile data (stock prices, live inventory)—route those via TTL = 0s bypass.
explanation.core: Decision Check: If cache evaluation p99 exceeds 12 ms or async shadow drift exceeds 1.5%, fail open directly to the Foundation Model Origin.
explanation.deepDive: Glossary: (1) Radix Trie: Compressed prefix tree for O(L) exact prefix matching; (2) SQ8: 8-bit scalar quantization reducing vector RAM 4x; (3) Cosine Distance tau: Upper bound on angular dissimilarity; (4) Model Epoch: Deployment version tag for O(1) lazy invalidation; (5) Slot Guard: Lexical check for numbers, dates, and negations.

decisionExercise.prompt: Your L2 cache hit rate jumps from 26% to 44% after an embedding model update, and users report wrong answers on date-sensitive queries. What is the fastest safe mitigation?

options.label: Tighten tau from 0.08 to 0.05 and verify Entity/Negation Slot Guard date extraction
options.feedback: Tightening tau and enforcing exact date slot matching immediately stops false-positive semantic hits without flushing L1.

options.label: Run FLUSHALL across all 100M cache entries
options.feedback: Flushing all 100M entries triggers a thundering herd that can overwhelm the origin GPU fleet.

steps.label: Normalize & Hash
steps.detail: Canonicalize prompt, apply HMAC(tenant_id, model_epoch), check L1 Radix Trie (<1 ms).

steps.label: ONNX INT8 Embed
steps.detail: On L1 miss, encode user turn into 384-d unit vector in <=4 ms.

steps.label: HNSW + Slot Guard
steps.detail: Query tenant-filtered SQ8 HNSW; accept only if d < 0.08 and entity/negation slots match.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must an L2 semantic cache pair cosine distance thresholding with an Entity/Negation Slot Guard?

options.feedback: Scalar quantization (SQ8) handles vector compression, not lexical polarity.

options.text: Because dense embeddings can score negations or different dates within d < 0.08
options.feedback: Correct—lexical inversions and numeric swaps often sit close in embedding space.
Tenant isolation is enforced via HMAC salting and Roaring Bitmap pre-filters.
RocksDB stores the compressed prompt-response payloads.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Dense embeddings capture topical similarity rather than exact logical polarity or numeric/date equality.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does model_epoch tagging avoid a thundering herd during LLM weight upgrades?

options.text: By deleting all 100M keys synchronously before deploy
options.feedback: Synchronous cluster-wide flushes cause GPU origin stampedes.

options.text: By bumping the global epoch in O(1) so stale entries miss lazily and compact in background
options.feedback: Correct—lazy O(1) invalidation avoids flush storms and reclaims space during compaction.

options.text: By disabling L1 Radix prefix matching permanently
options.feedback: L1 remains active under the new model_epoch.

options.text: By increasing cosine threshold tau to 0.25

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Bumping model_epoch lazily invalidates older entries on read in O(1) time.

knowledgeChecks.question: What happens if L2 HNSW evaluation latency exceeds the 12 ms circuit-breaker threshold?

options.feedback: A cache outage should never fail availability.

options.text: Fail open directly to the Foundation Model Origin
options.feedback: Correct—semantic caches must fail open so availability is preserved.

options.text: Serve a random cached response from another tenant

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Failing open preserves availability and bounds cache miss overhead.

knowledgeChecks.question: How much raw vector DRAM do 100M 384-d embeddings consume under 8-bit Scalar Quantization (SQ8)?

options.feedback: 153.6 GB is FP32 (4 bytes/dim), not SQ8.
Correct—100,000,000 * 384 * 1 byte = 38.4 GB before graph edges.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: SQ8 stores 1 byte per dimension, so 100M * 384 B = 38.4 GB.

beginner.summary: Combine exact prefix caching for repeated system prompts with vector similarity search for paraphrased user questions.
beginner.keyTakeaway: When users ask the same question in slightly different words, use vector similarity with a strict safety threshold to reuse answers fast.
beginner.byteSummary: LLM calls are slow and expensive. Instead of only caching exact text matches, a dual-tier cache checks exact prefixes first (<1 ms) and then checks if a similar question was already answered using embeddings.

intermediate.summary: Pair an L1 Radix Trie (<1 ms) with an L2 SQ8 HNSW index (tau=0.08) and lexical entity/negation guards under <15 ms p99.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: When building an LLM semantic cache, gate vector hits with cosine threshold tau=0.08 and exact entity/negation matching to prevent drift.
intermediate.byteSummary: L1 matches exact 256-token prefixes via XXH3-64. L2 encodes user turns with ONNX INT8 and searches tenant-filtered SQ8 HNSW in <6 ms, enforcing slot parity before serving cached RocksDB payloads.

advanced.summary: Architect a 15,000 RPS peak, 100M-entry dual-tier cache with HMAC tenant isolation, O(1) model-epoch invalidation, and closed-loop shadow drift control.
advanced.keyTakeaway: When scaling foundation model caching to 100M entries and 15K peak RPS, isolate tenants via HMAC-salted Roaring Bitmaps, invalidate via O(1) model_epoch tags, and fail open on >12 ms tail spikes.
advanced.byteSummary: 100M 384-d SQ8 vectors + HNSW edges fit in 110.7 GB DRAM (RF=2 across 8 shards) backed by 400 GB Zstd NVMe RocksDB. Async Kafka write-back and 5% shadow LLM judging dynamically tune tau without blocking streaming TTFT.
